category_title: Focused female students with low frequency of participation
minimal_context: The student is sitting in a circle in a locked classroom, tasked with reading or listening to a short text for a discussion.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Welcome to our first session. Please look at the short text in front of you. I will read it out loud to the circle so we can discuss it.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly and looks down) I don't have anything to say.

TUTOR: Can you try to explain what you know about this topic before we start?

STUDENT: I don't know anything about it. I've never heard of any of this stuff.

TUTOR: That's okay, just follow along with the text while I read it.

STUDENT: (Pushes the text away) I'm not going to read it, and I don't want to listen to it either. I'm just not going to talk.

options.A: The tutor provides opportunities to respond as a form of teacher attention during the session.
options.B: The tutor explicitly requests clarification or further examples to push the dialogue philosophically.
options.C: The tutor ignores the behavior, praises other students in the circle for their appropriate behavior, and advises peers to ignore the student.
options.D: The tutor provides a pressure vest as a sensory accommodation during the discussion.
